proposed_core_edits.reason: Clarifies that the panel class is defined by its displayed member properties and is not identified with any published comparison class.
Makes explicit the subset relation used in the one-sided broader-class converse without equating this local submodel to a published synthetic-control class.
Separates compact iid-Gaussian local honesty, on which attainment is proved, from uniform honesty over the full mixing panel class.

prose_updates.tldr: Predictor weighting changes both the donor face and the future counterfactual performance of a synthetic control. This paper identifies the entire population prediction-MSE graph from the stated block-stable fixed-rank panel, constructs a uniformly valid root-\(n\) same-panel band over the predictor simplex, and computes the exact compact-local iid-Gaussian minimax expected maximum width through finite KKT-cell, conic-distance, and primal--dual linear programs with certified vanishing error. Exact attainment is local to the specified Gaussian neighborhoods; the global projection band is validity-only. Every procedure uniformly honest over the full panel class nevertheless obeys the computed local lower bound because that honesty requirement contains the Gaussian paths.

project_justification.fill: The paper combines row-span completion, a joint block-mean and covariance expansion, exact shifted-QP inversion, critical-cone curve geometry, and certified finite primal and dual decision programs. Bidirectional vanishing-deficiency transfer between the observed iid-Gaussian panel and its Gaussian shift proves the matching compact-local lower bound and attainment. The broader mixing-class result is uniform validity of the global projection band; only the lower bound, not Gaussian-local attainment, transfers to every honesty class containing the Gaussian paths.

prose_updates.related_work: CanenSong2026SimplexWeight, Theorem 3.1, is a high-level fixed-objective result under uniform joint asymptotic normality, nondegeneracy, and variance consistency. Its explicit synthetic-control example instead uses repeated cross-sections with iid individuals within dates and positive group shares; the fixed-cross-section long panel here may instantiate the abstract theorem separately at a fixed predictor weight, but it is not that published example. VivesiBastida2022PredictorSelection studies an aggregate fixed-dimensional long panel with time-varying linear factors, oracle separation and injectivity, and an \(\ell_1\)-penalized bilevel predictor-selection objective, rather than this fixed-ridge block-stable class. CattaneoFengTitiunik2021PredictionIntervals allows a fixed-unit stationary weakly dependent time series but targets future-counterfactual and treatment-effect prediction intervals, not simultaneous inference for a population-MSE graph. FangSantos2019Directional explains the failure of ordinary bootstrap reasoning at nonsmooth maps. EvansHansenStark2005MinimaxConfidence, SchaferStark2009OptimalRegions, and ArmstrongKolesar2018OptimalInference provide related decision-theoretic architectures, but not the unrestricted externally randomized maximum-curve-width problem for a moving-KKT risk graph. FreybergerRai2018UniformBands studies bands induced by a nonrandom-shape set and develops its main approximation for weighted-area loss; no strict numerical separation from that work is asserted here. The present results are derived for the displayed panel class itself, not by identifying it with any of these published classes.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The global mixing-class band and the locally optimal Gaussian-neighborhood bands are different procedures. The global projection band \(C_n\) is proved uniformly valid but is not claimed to be globally minimax. Exact optimality and attainment concern fixed-dimensional, compact iid-Gaussian local neighborhoods with known spectrally separated rank, fixed positive ridge, stable block means, and a stable donor post regime. The converse is broader: any band sequence uniformly honest over the full panel class is honest on the contained Gaussian paths and must have compact-local scaled expected maximum width at least \(L_\alpha\). The reverse implication is not proved, so Gaussian-local attainment gives no global-class attainment claim. Unknown rank, growing dimensions, singleton-date predictors, post-factor drift, shrinking ridge, direct guarantees for the different objectives in Synth or SparseSC, and optimal inference for a corrected causal treatment effect remain outside scope.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The KKT atlas, critical-cone risk map, certified LP/SOCP approximation, bidirectional Gaussian-panel deficiency transfer, and compact-local minimax theorem are established in the core. The remaining limitation is one of scope rather than an open proof step: the projection band over the stationary mixing class is a validity construction only, whereas exact decision optimality and attainment are proved on compact iid-Gaussian local experiments. Uniform honesty over the larger class implies the same local lower bound, but the locally attaining Gaussian procedures have not been shown uniformly valid or attaining over that larger class. No compulsory positive cost from a face change and no strict separation from existing generic band theory is asserted.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem establishes the field-level payoff: certified finite decision programs, bidirectional Gaussian-panel transfer, a matching compact-local lower bound, and asymptotic attainment through moving donor faces. Its lower bound also yields the formal one-sided corollary for every procedure uniformly honest over the full panel class.
statement_notes.gap: Existing fixed-objective simplex inference and generic confidence-region results do not determine the unrestricted externally randomized maximum-curve-width value for this moving-KKT population-risk graph. This core now determines that value and transfers it sharply on the specified iid-Gaussian panel neighborhoods; what is not claimed is global mixing-class attainment by either the local rules or the validity-only projection band.
